attribution_limitations: Figure 6 caption places the retrospective EGD 5 years before the first biopsy and lanthanum start 6 months before that EGD, while the text says lanthanum had been taken for 5 years at biopsy (4 years after hemodialysis to 9 years after hemodialysis). The two intervals differ by about 6 months.

Position of the yellowish–white substance relative to vessels on magnified NBI is worded differently: "above enlarged regular vessels" (case report and Figure 1 caption), "subepithelial vessels were observed on the yellowish–white substance" (abstract), and "below the epithelial vessels" or "beneath the sub-epithelial capillary network" (discussion).

Follow-up endoscopic findings are described as "improved a little" at 3 years and 5 months after discontinuation (text and Figure 4 caption) but also as "no significant changes" with persistence of the findings in the discussion, and the abstract says the white rough mucosa "still exists". The discussion statement has no stated time.
The antral lesions are surrounded by "annular whitish mucosa" in the text but by "annular yellowish mucosa" in the Figure 1 caption.
The H. pylori antibody value 8.7 is printed with the unit IU/ml in the text and U/mL in Table 1.

The text says phosphate was elevated, while Table 1 labels the row P and the footnote defines P as phosphorous; the table value carries no high flag and the text statement is kept as a separate review_only item.

The case report says the aggregates were thought to reflect histiocyte phagocytosis of lanthanum (hedged), and parietal cell hyperplasia was "thought to be due to" lansoprazole; neither hedged cause is recorded as an asserted cause.
Table 1 and its text sentence give no collection time for the blood tests, and the Table 2 literature summary and pie chart describe 51 previously reported cases, not this patient.

claims.text: Nine years following hemodialysis, screening EGD showed whitish cobblestone-like mucosa in the gastric corpus and reddish depressed lesions with annular whitish mucosa in the antrum, and magnified NBI showed a yellowish–white substance within villous-like structures. Biopsies showed parietal cell hyperplasia and CD68-positive histiocyte aggregates. SEM–EDS detected lanthanum and phosphorus, mainly in histiocytes, confirming lanthanum deposition in the gastric mucosa; retrospective review showed whitish mucosa 6 months after lanthanum began.
